note: Curated resilience actions keyed by Köppen main group and a generic fallback. Sources are FAO, IPCC, WHO and national agencies. Language is 'helps reduce risk'; confirm with local experts before acting.

fallback.title: Sign up for official early warnings
fallback.why: A shifting climate zone changes which extremes are likely here.
fallback.action: Register for your national meteorological service's heat, flood and air-quality alerts and agree a household plan for each.
fallback.earlyWarning: Watch for multi-day heat, heavy-rain or air-quality advisories.

fallback.title: Use water efficiently and store some
fallback.why: Both wetter and drier futures stress local water supplies.
fallback.action: Fix leaks, add rainwater capture, and keep a few days of safe drinking water; helps reduce impact of supply disruption.
fallback.earlyWarning: Falling reservoir levels or hosepipe restrictions.

A.title: Flood-proof the home and documents
A.why: Tropical zones face heavier downpours and rising flood risk.
A.action: Raise electrics, keep sandbags/boards ready, and store IDs in a waterproof grab-bag; helps reduce flood losses.
A.earlyWarning: River gauges rising, repeated heavy-rain warnings.
A.evidenceNote: IPCC AR6 WGII: increased heavy precipitation in tropics.

A.title: Switch to heat- and flood-tolerant varieties
A.why: Hotter, wetter seasons raise crop disease and heat stress.
A.action: Adopt submergence-tolerant rice and improved drainage; stagger planting to spread risk. Helps reduce harvest loss.

A.title: Upgrade urban drainage and green space
A.why: Dense tropical cities flood when drains are overwhelmed.
A.action: Expand permeable surfaces, clear culverts before the wet season, and protect wetlands; helps reduce urban flooding.
A.earlyWarning: Recurrent surface flooding after short storms.

B.title: Make a hot-day plan and cool room
B.why: Arid zones are warming toward dangerous heat thresholds.
B.action: Identify a cool room, shift activity to morning/evening, hydrate, and check on elderly neighbours; helps prevent heat illness.
B.earlyWarning: Forecast highs above local heat-health threshold for 2+ days.

B.title: Drip irrigation and soil moisture capture
B.why: Less reliable rainfall and higher evaporation shrink water budgets.
B.action: Switch to drip lines, mulch, and drought-tolerant crops; schedule irrigation to soil-moisture data. Helps reduce water stress.
B.earlyWarning: Declining well levels, longer dry spells.
B.evidenceNote: FAO water productivity in dry regions.

B.title: Stabilise soils and track dust advisories
B.why: Expanding drylands raise dust storms and PM pollution.
B.action: Maintain vegetation buffers, issue dust advisories, and support mask access for outdoor workers; helps reduce respiratory exposure.
B.earlyWarning: Rising PM10/dust forecasts, bare exposed soil.
B.evidenceNote: WMO Sand and Dust Storm guidance.

C.title: Create defensible space and a go-bag
C.why: Temperate/Mediterranean zones face longer, drier fire seasons.
C.action: Clear vegetation near structures, prepare an evacuation go-bag, and agree a leave-early trigger; helps reduce fire injury and loss.
C.earlyWarning: Red-flag fire-weather warnings, prolonged dry heat.
C.evidenceNote: IPCC AR6 WGII: increased fire weather.

C.title: Adjust crop mix and water storage
C.why: Hotter summers push some crops past their comfort range.
C.action: Trial heat-tolerant cultivars, add on-farm storage, and shade-net sensitive crops; helps reduce yield loss.
C.earlyWarning: Earlier heat onset, reduced spring soil moisture.

C.title: Urban cooling and heat-health plan
C.why: Mild temperate cities are unprepared for new heat extremes.
C.action: Plant shade trees, open cooling centres, and publish a heat-health action plan; helps prevent heat deaths.
C.earlyWarning: Night-time temperatures staying high during heatwaves.

D.title: Prepare for heavier rain and snowmelt
D.why: Continental zones see more intense rain and faster thaw.
D.action: Check sump pumps, clear gutters, and keep an emergency kit; helps reduce flood damage and outages.
D.earlyWarning: Rapid spring warming over deep snowpack.

D.title: Use the longer, warmer growing season carefully
D.why: Warming extends the season but adds heat and pest risk.
D.action: Trial longer-maturing varieties with irrigation backup and monitor new pests; helps stabilise yields.
D.earlyWarning: Earlier last-frost dates, new pest sightings.

D.title: Harden infrastructure for swings
D.why: Continental zones face both heat and sharp cold extremes.
D.action: Insulate critical infrastructure, plan for grid peaks, and update building codes for both extremes; helps reduce outages.
D.earlyWarning: More frequent record-high and record-low days.

E.title: Monitor ground stability
E.why: Warming polar/tundra ground destabilises foundations and roads.
E.action: Inspect foundations for tilting, report road slumps, and follow community relocation guidance; helps reduce structural risk.
E.earlyWarning: Cracking walls, uneven ground, sinking posts.

E.title: Adapt infrastructure to thawing ground
E.why: Thaw undermines roads, pipelines and buildings on permafrost.
E.action: Use thermosyphons/elevated foundations, re-survey routes, and plan managed retreat where needed; helps protect lifelines.
E.earlyWarning: Accelerating ground subsidence and coastal erosion.
